description.narrative: The proposed IDF Grant is to support the strategy of the Beninese government to combat financial crime and more specifically money laundering and terrorist financing, by helping institutions with a stake in the fight against those two forms of crimes to build up management and operational capacity and effectiveness on anti-money laundering and combating financing of terrorism (AML/CFT). The components of the grant are expected to play an important role in spearheading this objective by helping the Beninese authorities to: (i) reinforce the operational capacities of the Cellule Nationale des Information Financiè res (CENTIF), the Financial Intelligence Unit responsible for receiving, analyzing and processing suspicious transaction reports; (ii) enhance compliance with AML/CFT legal obligations; and (iii) strengthening the law enforcement response to AML/CFT. The objective of the project is to improve the reporting, analysis, and investigation of suspicious transaction reports (STRs) by the private sector and key Government agencies involved in anti-money laundering and counter-terrorism financing (AML/CFT) in Benin, including the judiciary. This will be achieved by: - reinforcing the operational capacities of the financial intelligence unit (FIU), the Cellule Nationale pour le Traitement des Informations Financières (CENTIF) to analyze suspicious transaction reports (STRs) filed by the private sector; - improving the reporting of STRs by the private sector and - ensuring an adequate handling of money laundering and financial crime cases by the judiciary.

title.narrative: Number of Suspicious Transaction Reports (STR) filed by the non banks and non-financial Reporting Entities

comment.narrative: the final supervision mission for this IDF will take place in June 2014. Receiving 10 new STRs as a result of the capacity buildingactivities organized is a reasonable target.

At the time of the supervision mission, the CENTIF was not playing its role as the driver of the AML/CFT regime - contacts withtheprivate sector were discontinued. This contact was resumed with the preparation of the guidelines for financial andnon-financial institutions, which included awareness raising activities and private sector consultations on challenges faced inimplementing AML/CFTmeasures

title.narrative: Number of STRs analyzed by the CENTIF

comment.narrative: the final supervision mission for this IDF will take place in June 2014. CENTIF is currently implementing its new procedure manualand has committed to reviewing its entire STR stock, as well as analyze new STR received.

Situation of blockage within CENTIF at the time of the supervision mission. STRs were not being analyzed and therefore none wastransmitted to the public prosecutor. An emergency plan has been developed for STR analysis with the implementation of the newprocedure manual of the CENTIF
